item-13|ds.raw: Hi everyone! I am glad to release the two 18th-century British pianos - The 1796 Broadwood Baby grand and the 1781 Ganer square piano virtual libraries for decent sampler via Pianobook, developed for my Postgraduate (taught) Project. The samples were recorded inside the anechoic chamber at ISVR, University of Southampton, United Kingdom, where the Professor, musician and composer David Owen Norris contributed to the recordings, which were later used for physics-based modelling and comparisons. It is a collaborative project between the Institute of Sound and Vibration Research and the University of Southampton's Music Department. There are three variations for Broadwood (pedals): > No Pedals (F0 - key switches), > with Una Corda Pedal (G0), > with Sustain Pedal (A0) and there are 8 variations for the Ganer square piano (the dampers and buff stops): > No dampers; no buff stop (C0), > No dampers with.

item-65|ds.name: Austrian Jaw Harp
item-65|ds.raw: The Jaw Harp, also called the Juice Harp, Mouth Harp, or the Jew's Harp is a fun one note instrument. By striking a netal tong between two metal extrusions framing either side of the tong, and placing the frame against your teeth, you can generate a tone that is amplified by your open mouth. By changing the position of your lips and toungue you can further change the tone of the note. This VST I have created, while simple, is still a lot of fun and is silly. Hopefully you all enjoy it as much as I do!

item-101|ds.name: Cinematic Granular Synthesizer
item-101|ds.raw: Cinematic Granular Synth Creator: Trevor Venemon-Holt Over the last two months, I went through this phase of modular synthesis. Not having enough money for my own Eurorack hardware, I asked chat, GPT, what are some software alternatives and it pointed me towards VCV rack, a perfect hardware emulator, and you can record the patches that you make as an audio or video file and use them for songs. So I designed my own patch in VCV Rack, using two main oscillators, a texture, synthesizer for granular synthesis, and then built-in effects from DecentSampler. I used it in a project and one thing that the sample preset does it even better is capture all of the qualities from each individual sample. When I used it in a song, the texture synthesizer was monophonic, but when I sampled it, it would become polyphonic, which is an added bonus I didn’t think about at first.

Giacomo **Date:** October 29, 2023 **By:** Oliver Scheuch ## Included Formats - Decent Sampler ## Release Notes **First Release** ## The Story and Usage Introducing a unique sample pack inspired by my recent journey to Tuscany – the "Coro di Cicale" featuring the remarkable. item-11|ds.name: NFO Alternative Chamber Strings Longs Marco Iannello
item-11|ds.raw: In the middle of April 2021, I had booked a 3 hour slot part of a shared recording session offered by Manchester based Northern Film Orchestra, in order to record a few ambient, textural chamber strings cues for a short film I had been scoring. As the players were so incredibly brilliant, the recordings were wrapped up halfway through the session, and I had previously asked Jack Hughes, director of the NFO, whether I could capture a few samples of the chamber strings ensemble, with the objective of making a sample. Jack had happily agreed to that , so we went ahead and started sampling both long and short notes, starting from the lowest C0 and going up in 5ths to F6.The long samples were recorded twice, whereas the short ones were recorded four times. I had time to record only a single dynamic layer, which I decided to be mezzoforte. In the end, I was sent about 3 gigabytes of samples, and I decided to use the Close, Stereo Pair, Outriggers, and Room ones, therefore, for this reason, the library features four mic positions.

item-287|ds.raw: # Santa Croce Soundscapes Sample Pack The "Santa Croce Soundscapes" sample pack is the result of recordings made during my stay in Tuscany at the impressive Santa Croce Church in Florence. item-331|ds.name: Thunder & Wine
item-331|ds.raw: # Thunder & Wine Sample Pack - Version: 1.0 Name: Oliver Scheuch ## Included formats - Decent Sampler ## Description While capturing the sound of a wine glass might not be groundbreaking, I believe in starting small and I just wanted to make a humble contribution to this. ## First Preset: Thunder & Wine I recorded a wine glass with precision using an Octawa MK12 microphone, placing it on a stereo track. This unassuming sound is then enveloped in a Convolution Hall created from a 20-second thunder recording captured in my garden a few days ago. item-363|ds.name: Yogurt
item-363|ds.raw: # [Yogurt] Version: [1.1] ## Included formats - Decent Sampler ## The Story One day, I was eating a yogurt. I hit the bottom of the plastic pot with my spoon, and it made a lovely, percussive sound. I decided to record it and then I tried to give it more shape by layering a sine wave and a square wave, with some ADSR and LFO shenanigans. Many hours later, the original sound has been sent through several reverb and modulation pedals to give birth to six different flavors, going from the cleanest to the weirdest. I hope you have as much fun playing with Yogurt as I had making it !
